instruction: Ensure exactly two applications remain in your favorites: Vim and the web browser.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.click({SCREEN_WIDTH_HALF}, {SCREEN_HEIGHT_HALF}); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires removing Thunderbird while keeping Chrome and Vim. Uses existing check_gnome_favorite_apps metric to verify exactly two apps remain.

Metric logic correct: check_gnome_favorite_apps parses the string, checks count (exactly 2), and verifies content using set comparison
Complete coverage: instruction requires exactly 2 apps (Vim and browser) - metric verifies both count and identity
Expected values semantically correct: vim.desktop and google-chrome.desktop correctly correspond to 'Vim' and 'web browser' mentioned in instruction
Data flow correct: Framework calls get_rule which returns rules dict directly; metric correctly accesses rule['expected']
Set-based comparison handles order independence: both ['vim.desktop', 'google-chrome.desktop'] and ['google-chrome.desktop', 'vim.desktop'] pass
No state dependencies: gsettings command is always accessible without requiring UI/dialog state; no postconfig needed
Edge cases handled: metric checks length before content comparison, preventing index errors
